title: Implement core encode/decode byte transform
description:
Implement src/transform.rs: the yEnc byte-level encode and decode operations.

ENCODE:
  pub(crate) fn encode_bytes(input: &[u8], line_length: u8, output: &mut Vec<u8>)

Algorithm per byte:
1. encoded = input_byte.wrapping_add(42)
2. If encoded is NUL(0x00), LF(0x0A), CR(0x0D), or =(0x3D): write 0x3D then encoded.wrapping_add(64)
3. Otherwise: write encoded
4. Track column count; when column reaches line_length, write \r\n and reset column

Note: the spec says to also escape TAB and SPACE in some old versions. Do NOT escape them -- modern encoders do not and it wastes space.

DECODE:
  pub(crate) fn decode_bytes(input: &[u8], output: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), YencError>

Algorithm:
- Process input bytes sequentially
- Discard CR (0x0D), LF (0x0A), NUL (0x00) -- these are line-wrap artifacts
- When = (0x3D) is encountered: read next non-CRLF byte X, emit X.wrapping_sub(64).wrapping_sub(42)
- Otherwise: emit byte.wrapping_sub(42)
- Stop when a line beginning with =yend is reached (caller handles this; this function processes the data bytes only between =ybegin/=ypart and =yend)

Dot-stuffing: if the first byte of a line (position immediately after LF) is . (0x2E), check if the next byte is also . -- if so, skip the first dot (it was transport dot-stuffing). This is a defensive heuristic; do not add dots to encoded output.

Build a lookup table at compile time (const fn) for the encode path to avoid branches in the hot loop. The aswaving/yenc crate demonstrates this pattern.

Tests (oracle: hand-computed from the algorithm, or use Python: bytes([((b + 42) % 256) for b in input_bytes]) for encode):
- Encode b'Cat' -> known output bytes (compute manually or via Python)
- Encode byte that maps to NUL -> escape sequence present in output
- Encode byte that maps to = -> escape sequence present in output
- Encode byte that maps to LF -> escape sequence present in output
- Encode byte that maps to CR -> escape sequence present in output
- Decode the above outputs -> original bytes
- Decode with CRLF line endings -> CRLF discarded, data correct
- Decode with dot-stuffing (.. at line start) -> single dot emitted
- Round-trip: encode then decode = identity for all byte values 0x00-0xFF
close_reason: Implemented in decode.rs:decode_line and encode.rs:encode_body. Core +42/-42 transform, escape handling, dot-stuffing, CRLF discard. 9 unit tests + all-256-bytes round-trip.
